tasks.short: Check travel availability and allocate the customer's chosen space.

steps.what: Capture dates, passenger details and preferences in the {OTHER} reservation system.
Check live capacity and allocation restrictions in the {OTHER} reservation system.
Explain available options and agree alternatives when requested spaces are unavailable.
Allocate the agreed space in the {OTHER} reservation system after customer approval.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake, availability filters and allocation rules in the {OTHER} reservation system. Recheck inventory when committing the customer's approved selection, prevent duplicate allocations and pass the reservation record to the confirmation workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing booking functions may cover availability, but intake, supplier inventories and allocation rules are often configured separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reservation controls can handle the structured work. AI-assisted coding makes missing adapters cheaper to build; it does not create supplier access.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier inventory can change between search and commitment. Group allocations, accessibility requirements and inconsistent supplier restrictions need exception handling.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the customer can compromise on when the requested journey is unavailable.

ambition.what: Flexible-date alternatives during the first customer contact

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time searching and entering allocations, and more time resolving constrained journeys. They can offer approved alternatives immediately; pricing and compensation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve unavailable-booking inquiries using approved alternatives.
reach.learn: Inventory freshness, allocation restrictions and the limits of a temporary hold.

evidence.claim: Structured availability checks and allocations can use deterministic reservation controls.
Mews supports hotel self-service and automated charge routing, adjacent to this reservation workflow.

assumptions: The baseline is a staffed travel desk using an existing reservation system.
That system supports live searches, configured allocation rules and safe commitment.
The structured-input prior fits this task; API availability remains unconfirmed.
Customer approval covers the exact selection and any disclosed commitment.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates for one reservation-system connection.
GDPR applies to passenger records. Access and any employee consultation under national rules are included in consent_and_access.
unknowns: Whether the desk books transport, lodging or both.
Which inventory sources expose supported search and allocation interfaces.
Whether holds, duplicate prevention and atomic allocation are supported.
How often group requests or accessibility constraints require intervention.
Which configuration rights and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which existing configuration can replace manual searching without new code?
How does the reservation interface handle expired availability, retries and partial group allocations?
new_work: Handle stale inventory and failed allocations.
Maintain allocation restrictions and supplier mappings.
Check duplicate prevention and inventory freshness after interface changes.

tasks.short: Confirm reservations and tell customers or travel agents about transport changes.

steps.what: Match change notices to affected reservations in the {OTHER} reservation system.
Prepare confirmation or change messages from approved templates in the {EMAIL}.
Send routine reservation confirmations through the {EMAIL}.
Check and send consequential travel-change notices through the {EMAIL}.
Call customers or travel agents to explain changes and discuss their needs.
Record notification status and contact outcomes in the {OTHER} reservation system.

tasks.design: Connect structured events from the {OTHER} reservation system to configured templates and delivery tracking in the {EMAIL} and {WORKFLOW}. Send routine confirmations automatically, require agent approval for consequential change notices, and queue unresolved cases for human calls through the {TELEPHONY}. Log delivery events automatically and use a short form for call outcomes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Change notices, reservation records and contact histories often sit in separate places. Staff manually identify recipients and track responses.
tasks.enabler_now: Event matching, templates, approval routing and delivery tracking are established capabilities. Small deterministic adapters can connect them.
tasks.still_hard: Delivery does not prove that a passenger understood the change. Missed connections, conflicting supplier notices and urgent disruption calls remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Calm distressed travellers, explain practical consequences and negotiate a workable response.
tasks.altitude: The agent's week shifts from recipient matching and message preparation to unresolved disruptions. They gain discretion to prioritise callbacks within agreed urgency criteria.

reach.task: Prioritise disruption callbacks across the support queue.
reach.learn: Delivery status, acknowledgement limits and journey urgency.

evidence.claim: Event matching and template-based reservation notifications need no model.
Zendesk supports customer communication and integrated record actions; transport disruption handling is not established by this source.
An NBER support-agent study found improved issue resolution with an assistant; it does not establish savings for this task.

assumptions: Change notices arrive as structured reservation events; unstructured notices remain exceptions.
Routine confirmations and consequential change notices follow different approval paths.
The communication prior fits disruption calls, but preparation and delivery are separately automatable.
The solution does not record or transcribe calls.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for one reservation connection and one notification channel.
GDPR applies to recipient data. Access and employee consultation under national rules, where applicable, are included.
unknowns: Whether supplier changes include stable journey and reservation identifiers.
Which notices require approval under current service policy.
Whether contact records distinguish customers from authorised travel agents.
Which delivery and acknowledgement events are available.
Which employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can duplicate or superseded supplier notices be detected before sending?
Which existing configuration supports approvals, failed-delivery retries and callback queues?
new_work: Resolve failed delivery, missing contacts and conflicting changes.
Maintain templates, urgency criteria and recipient mappings.
Enter concise call outcomes and monitor unresolved callbacks.

tasks.short: Recommend and promote destinations, tour packages and travel services.

steps.what: Ask customers about budget, interests, dates and practical constraints.
Compare suitable packages in the {OTHER} reservation system against customer requirements.
Explain package trade-offs and respond to customer concerns.
Draft a tailored package summary in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Approved package facts, current terms and agent-entered customer preferences.
loop.output: A short package summary with references to supplied facts.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates, inclusions and links against supplied records; the agent checks suitability before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair within 30 seconds; use a fixed template or manual draft on failure.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates remain the default. A bounded drafting loop handles explanations tailored to free-text concerns without maintaining many template variants.

steps.what: Check claims, prices and contact permission, then send the summary through the {EMAIL}.
Record customer interest and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure package filters in the {OTHER} reservation system and concise preference capture in the {CRM}. Generate factual summaries from templates, using a bounded drafting loop only for tailored explanations, and require agent approval before sending through the {EMAIL}. Create follow-up tasks from the recorded customer response and permitted contact purpose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogue facts and customer preferences are separated, while tailored explanations take writing time. Software can filter packages but cannot establish customer trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured filters handle factual matching. Bounded drafting can turn approved facts and customer concerns into an editable summary.
tasks.still_hard: Travel suitability depends on unstated expectations. Availability, package claims and contact permissions must remain current.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what matters to the traveller and explain trade-offs without pressuring them into an unsuitable purchase.

ambition.what: Written trade-off summary for undecided travellers

tasks.altitude: The agent spends more time advising and less time searching or composing follow-ups. They gain discretion over how to explain approved packages, while discounts and package terms retain existing approval limits.

reach.task: Prepare travel follow-ups from approved package facts.
reach.learn: Package inclusions, claim verification and permitted contact purposes.

evidence.claim: Deterministic filters can shortlist packages using dates, budget and explicit requirements.
bol's Shophulp provides conversational product advice; the digest identifies it as a beta, not a travel-advice case.
Drafting a reply from a case record with clerk approval is an established assistive pattern.

assumptions: The baseline is individual advice and follow-up, rather than ownership of mass campaigns.
Package facts and prices are available in structured records.
The relationship and low-rule-coverage priors fit the advisory conversation; factual shortlisting is more structured.
Model use is internal drafting. No customer-facing chatbot is introduced.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for a limited package catalogue.
GDPR, applicable contact-marketing rules and EU AI Act obligations apply. National employee consultation requirements are checked where relevant.
unknowns: Whether package records include reliable inclusions, exclusions and current prices.
Whether customer preferences are already captured in the {CRM}.
Which follow-ups are requested service messages and which are marketing.
How often a fixed template would cover the desired summary.
Which approved model-processing arrangements and consultation requirements exist.
research_questions: Do configured filters and templates cover most advice preparation without a model?
Can every variable claim in a tailored summary be traced to a current package record?
new_work: Maintain package facts, filters and templates.
Handle missing terms, expired prices and uncertain contact permissions.
Sample drafts for unsupported claims and maintain the bounded drafting instructions.

tasks.short: Keep the information desk and customer area clean during service.

steps.what: Inspect the information desk and customer area for dirt, spills and obstructions.
Wipe surfaces, remove ordinary litter and leave customer routes clear.
Report hazards or cleaning beyond desk duties through the {CHAT}.

tasks.design: Keep inspection and cleaning as physical work, with supplies close to the information desk. Configure a short location-and-hazard reporting template in the {CHAT} so the facilities team receives usable requests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Software cannot wipe surfaces or remove litter. Reporting can be simplified, but it is a small part of this task.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication templates can reduce incomplete cleaning requests. No technical breakthrough changes the physical work.
tasks.still_hard: Spills arise unpredictably during customer service. Safe cleaning depends on local conditions, suitable supplies and timely facilities support.
tasks.human_edge: Notice immediate hazards and keep the area usable while helping passengers.
tasks.altitude: The person's week and decision rights barely change. Reporting takes slightly less time; inspection and cleaning remain part of the shift.

reach.task: Report cleaning hazards in shared customer areas.
reach.learn: Safe isolation, location details and the boundary between desk cleaning and specialist work.

evidence.claim: Cleaning a staffed information area is predominantly physical work; a reporting template offers only a small administrative gain.

assumptions: The agent performs light cleaning; specialist or hazardous cleaning goes to the facilities team.
The screen, API and confidentiality priors do not describe the main physical work.
The baseline uses the {CHAT} for occasional facilities requests.
No monitoring, cameras or new employee performance records are introduced.
Shares average routine cleaning and occasional escalation; estimates require local validation.
GDPR applies if requests contain personal data. Existing access and applicable national consultation rules are checked during setup.
unknowns: Which cleaning duties belong to the desk role.
Which hazards require specialist attendance.
Whether supplies are readily available.
Which facilities reporting channel is used today.
Whether the existing channel supports a reusable request template.
research_questions: Would better supply placement save more time than changing the reporting process?
What minimum location and hazard details let the facilities team act without clarification?
new_work: Maintain the facilities contact and reporting template.
Check that unresolved hazards receive attention.

role.altitude: Routine availability checks, allocation entry and notification preparation shrink. The role centres more on constrained journeys, disruption recovery and trusted travel advice, with callback prioritisation within agreed limits.
reach: Customer service representatives: handle booking exceptions using current reservation and contact records.
First-line supervisors: prioritise unresolved disruption callbacks.
Correspondence clerks: prepare accurate travel follow-ups from approved facts.
Receptionists: report shared-area hazards with usable location details.
skills_to_grow: Interpret allocation restrictions and inventory freshness.
Explain journey and package trade-offs clearly.
Handle distressed travellers and disruption exceptions.
Verify generated claims against current package facts.
Use contact permissions and concise case records correctly.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a journey-recovery desk that combines approved alternatives, urgent callbacks and clear written options, with the agent authorised to prioritise time-critical cases.

job.title: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
